title: Patterned Wafer Inspection - Voids Detection on Zeta-388
subtitle: Post-Lithography Quality Validation for 28nm Node Manufacturing
author: Emily Nakamura

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the Zeta-388 system to detect and classify Voids defects during post-lithography inspection at the 28nm technology node. The test is conducted at Singapore Fab 7 to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 200mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for Voids defects that are critical to yield at the 28nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the Zeta-388 platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: Zeta-388
- Inspection Type: Patterned Wafer Inspection
- Target Defect: Voids
- Process Step: Post-Lithography
- Wafer Size: 200mm
- Technology Node: 28nm
- Fab Location: Singapore Fab 7

This test case applies to all Zeta-388 systems deployed at Singapore Fab 7 for post-lithography monitoring in the 28nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: Zeta-388
Software Version: v12.8.398
Recipe: PATTERNED_WAFER_INSPECTION_28nm_POST_LITHOGRAPHY
Illumination Mode: Darkfield
Scan Speed: High (70 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 0.5μm
Edge Exclusion: 5mm
Sampling Plan: Full wafer sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the Zeta-388 system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'Patterned Wafer Inspection' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target Voids defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 28nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 82 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 98% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±2.5% for Patterned Wafer Inspection
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.96 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2025-02-20
Wafers Tested: 14
Total Defects Found: 4649
Defect Density: 1479.82 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 2.2%
Capture Rate: 97.0%
Test Duration: 441 minutes
System Uptime: 98.2%

Result Classification: PASS
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Zeta-388 demonstrated excellent performance in detecting Voids at the 28nm node.

b) The capture rate exceeded the minimum threshold, confirming system readiness.

c) Nuisance rate is within acceptable limits.

d) Throughput metrics met production requirements without sensitivity compromise.

e) The defect review station correlation was within specification.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS: No corrective actions required. Test passed all acceptance criteria.
